governanceNotes: D1 batch 78 (2026-09-27): one bounded association edge authored - renal-toxicity to chronic-kidney-disease (rank 1) - classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, hypothesizedOnly:true, mechanismCategory PHARMACOLOGICAL_IATROGENIC. The edge rests on the Swedish active-comparator register cohort of 10,946 initiators (therapeutic-dose comparison null at hazard ratio 1.11 carried openly as the anchor's own counterweight; toxic-range lithium associated with chronic kidney disease progression hazard ratio 2.86 and acute kidney injury hazard ratio 3.51, PMID 37418264), the cisplatin longitudinal cohort of 2,191 patients (injury in 4.2 percent of 8,482 cycles predicting long-term renal dysfunction, PMID 36941500), and the tenofovir retrospective cohort of 182 adults (early nephrotoxicity to chronic kidney disease in 34.6 percent over 5 years, PMID 40811628), with the exposure-specific and comorbidity-attribution limits carried openly. The aristolochic-acid urothelial-carcinoma window is recorded as a direction-guarded withholding with reserved anchors (PMIDs 10841870, 12505369, 25025033): the genotoxic-adduct mechanism defeats the condition-to-cancer arrow and the uremic route is chain-owned by the chronic-kidney-disease window. One additional searched anchor preserved as corroborating material (not registered; three-reference cap): the Mayo Clinic historical cohort documenting chronic kidney disease in 27 percent of 154 long-term lithium patients with comorbidity-attributed progression (PMID 33548063).

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Renal toxicity associates with chronic kidney disease at population-register and exposure-cohort level with the toxic-exposure gradient as the quantified signal: the Swedish new-user active-comparator cohort of 10,946 mood-disorder patients documents NO excess chronic kidney disease risk at therapeutic lithium exposure versus valproate (hazard ratio 1.11, 95 percent CI 0.86-1.45; 10-year chronic kidney disease risk 8.4 versus 8.2 percent) as an explicit counterweight, while lithium levels in the toxic range (above 1.0 mmol per liter) associate with chronic kidney disease progression (hazard ratio 2.86, 95 percent CI 0.97-8.45) and acute kidney injury (hazard ratio 3.51, 95 percent CI 1.41-8.76) (PMID 37418264), the cisplatin longitudinal cohort of 2,191 solid-tumor patients across 8,482 treatment cycles documents cisplatin-induced kidney injury in 4.2 percent of cycles and identifies it as a significant independent predictor of long-term renal dysfunction (annualized eGFR decline, P<0.01) (PMID 36941500), and the tenofovir retrospective cohort of 182 antiretroviral-treated adults documents early nephrotoxicity significantly associated with chronic kidney disease within 5 years (63 of 182 patients, 34.6 percent; incidence 69.2 per 1,000 person-years) (PMID 40811628); recorded as documented association only with the exposure-specific limits carried openly and the null-anchor discipline applied - the anchors carry positive toxic-injury signal with the therapeutic-dose null stated on the record, and the identity's exposure population is the toxic-injury cohort.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of chronic-kidney-disease is established for any individual: the located evidence is exposure-specific (lithium, cisplatin, and tenofovir carry distinct tubular and interstitial mechanisms and generalization to all nephrotoxins is untested), therapeutic-dose lithium showed NO excess risk in the active-comparator register cohort (the counterweight is the anchor's own result), progression attribution is confounded by diabetes, hypertension, and baseline renal reserve (risk factors in the located cohorts include hypertension, thoracic and liver malignancies, and baseline creatinine), and the acute-injury to chronic-disease transition is not separable from underlying renal comorbidity in retrospective designs; individual claims require dated renal-function and exposure-dose records with diabetic nephropathy, hypertensive nephrosclerosis, glomerular disease, obstructive uropathy, and pre-existing chronic kidney disease excluded.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Direct tubular and interstitial toxic injury - proximal-tubule atrophy with progressive interstitial fibrosis and nephron loss - is hypothesized to transition acute toxic insults into sustained glomerular-filtration decline meeting chronic kidney disease criteria, the fibrosis route supported by the toxic-range lithium gradient (progression hazard 2.86 with levels above 1.0 mmol per liter) and the cisplatin injury-to-dysfunction prediction and the early-nephrotoxicity-to-chronic-kidney-disease hazard in the tenofovir cohort, but whether the route produced any individual's chronic kidney disease remains hypothesized until exposure-dose and renal-function timelines are reviewed side by side.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at population-register plus exposure-cohort class with the null-counterweight and exposure-specific limits carried openly, following the nephritis to chronic-kidney-disease progression convention: the active-comparator register cohort quantifies the toxic-range gradient while documenting a therapeutic-dose null (PMID 37418264), the cisplatin cohort quantifies injury-to-long-term-dysfunction prediction in 2,191 patients (PMID 36941500), and the tenofovir cohort quantifies early-nephrotoxicity-to-chronic-kidney-disease hazard over 5 years (PMID 40811628); the null-anchor discipline is applied explicitly - positive toxic-injury signal with the therapeutic-dose null (hazard ratio 1.11, 95 percent CI 0.86-1.45) carried openly and the identity's toxic-injury population stated; because the evidence is exposure-specific with comorbidity-confounded progression attribution, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only with those limits stated and routes individual claims through dated exposure-dose and renal-function records with competing nephropathies excluded.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: The located quantification covers three named exposures (lithium, cisplatin, tenofovir) with distinct mechanisms and no located cohort spans nephrotoxic exposures generally; the register cohort's own primary comparison is null at therapeutic exposure and its toxic-range subgroup is small (3 percent of routine lithium tests were in the toxic range) with a progression confidence interval crossing 1 (0.97-8.45); the cisplatin cohort is retrospective single-center with injury defined per KDIGO criteria in a cancer population carrying independent renal risk; the tenofovir cohort is small (182 patients) and single-country; and the acute-injury to chronic-disease transition is not isolable from underlying renal comorbidity in any located design.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: diabetic nephropathy and hypertensive nephrosclerosis producing chronic kidney disease in exposed patients (risk-factor overlap documented in the located cohorts)
pre-existing chronic kidney disease at exposure baseline (dated baseline eGFR and creatinine required in individual claims)
obstructive uropathy, glomerular disease, and renovascular disease as competing chronic nephropathies
malignancy and its therapy as combined renal insult (the cisplatin cohort population carries tumor-related renal risk; the kidney-cancer window owns its sources)
volume depletion and sepsis-associated kidney injury during the exposure period

evidenceGaps: The located quantification covers three named exposures (lithium, cisplatin, tenofovir) with distinct mechanisms and no located cohort spans nephrotoxic exposures generally; the register cohort's own primary comparison is null at therapeutic exposure and its toxic-range subgroup is small (3 percent of routine lithium tests were in the toxic range) with a progression confidence interval crossing 1 (0.97-8.45); the cisplatin cohort is retrospective single-center with injury defined per KDIGO criteria in a cancer population carrying independent renal risk; the tenofovir cohort is small (182 patients) and single-country; and the acute-injury to chronic-disease transition is not isolable from underlying renal comorbidity in any located design.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at population-register plus exposure-cohort class with the null-counterweight and exposure-specific limits carried openly, following the nephritis to chronic-kidney-disease progression convention: the Swedish active-comparator cohort (PMID 37418264) quantifies the toxic-range progression gradient (hazard ratio 2.86) while its therapeutic-dose comparison is null (hazard ratio 1.11, 0.86-1.45 - carried openly as the anchor's own counterweight), the cisplatin cohort (PMID 36941500) documents kidney injury predicting long-term renal dysfunction in 2,191 patients, and the tenofovir cohort (PMID 40811628) documents early nephrotoxicity preceding chronic kidney disease in 34.6 percent over 5 years; the null-anchor discipline is applied - the toxic-injury subgroup is the identity's exposure population and the therapeutic-dose null is stated on the record; because the evidence is exposure-specific and progression attribution is comorbidity-confounded, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only and routes individual claims through dated exposure-dose and renal-function records with competing nephropathies excluded.

sourceReferences.note: Swedish new-user active-comparator register cohort (JAMA Netw Open 2023): 10,946 lithium or valproate initiators; chronic kidney disease risk NOT increased at therapeutic lithium exposure (HR 1.11, 95% CI 0.86-1.45; 10-year risk 8.4% vs 8.2%) - counterweight carried openly; toxic-range lithium (above 1.0 mmol/L) associated with CKD progression (HR 2.86, 95% CI 0.97-8.45) and acute kidney injury (HR 3.51, 95% CI 1.41-8.76); supports the bounded toxic-injury association only (small toxic-range subgroup).
